groups.title: A changing neighbourhood
groups.text:
A. In 2018, residents of Elmbridge turned an unused car park into a community garden. The council lent the land for five years, but the residents paid for tools themselves. They initially wanted a quiet place to grow vegetables. By the second summer, the garden had become a meeting place for people who rarely spoke to one another before.

B. Water was the first practical difficulty. The nearest tap was inside a locked building. Rather than buy expensive irrigation equipment, volunteers fitted tanks to collect rain from the roof of a nearby shed. This reduced their need for tap water, although they still used it during long dry periods.

C. A local researcher interviewed forty residents before the garden opened and a year later. More people reported knowing their neighbours after the project began. However, the study had no comparison group, so the researcher warned that the garden alone could not be credited with every change. She did not measure air temperature or property prices.

D. In 2023, the council renewed the land agreement for another five years. It declined a proposal to charge visitors, because free access had been a condition of the original agreement. A small weekend market now helps to cover the cost of seeds. Money from the market is used for the garden, not distributed to volunteers.

questions.prompt: The garden was created on land formerly used for parking.
questions.explanation: Paragraph A describes an unused car park.

questions.prompt: The council bought the residents their tools.
questions.explanation: Residents paid for the tools themselves.

questions.prompt: The garden reduced summer air temperatures.
questions.explanation: The researcher did not measure temperature; no result is given.
Paragraph B: volunteers fitted tanks.
Paragraph C specifies forty residents.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph describes a limitation of the research?
questions.explanation: Paragraph C: no comparison group.

questions.prompt: Why was a visitor fee rejected?
options: B. The agreement required free access.
C. The market had already closed.
questions.explanation: Paragraph D gives free access as an original condition.
Paragraph D states that the market covers the cost of seeds.

groups.title: Course notice
groups.text: The Riverside Learning Centre will run a photography course from 6 November to 18 December. Lessons take place on Thursday evenings, from six to eight. Students must bring a phone or camera; computers are provided at the centre. The course costs sixty pounds, including printing. Registration closes on 30 October. There are twelve places. Complete beginners are welcome, but students under sixteen must attend with an adult.

questions.prompt: On which day are the lessons?
questions.explanation: The notice says Thursday evenings.
Computers are provided.
The notice specifies twelve places.

questions.prompt: An experienced photographer teaches the course.
questions.explanation: The notice gives no information about the teacher.

groups.title: A quieter journey
groups.text: Last year, Maya began cycling to work instead of driving. The journey takes fifteen minutes longer, but she says she arrives feeling calmer. She bought a second-hand bicycle, which needed new lights but no other repairs. At first she avoided the main road because of traffic. In May, the town opened a protected cycle lane, and she changed her route. She still takes the bus in heavy rain. Maya would like to cycle at weekends too, but she currently uses that time to look after her grandfather.

options: A. She feels calmer when she arrives.
B. It is fifteen minutes faster.
C. Her office has banned cars.
questions.explanation: She arrives feeling calmer, although the journey is longer.
New lights were the only repairs needed.
The text specifies May.

questions.prompt: What prevents Maya from cycling at weekends?
options: C. She looks after a relative.
questions.explanation: She uses weekends to look after her grandfather.

groups.title: Library registration
groups.script: Good morning. I would like to join the library. Certainly. What is your surname? It is Benton. B E N T O N. Thank you. Which branch will you use? The branch on River Street. Fine. Our standard card is free, but printing costs twenty pence a page. I do not need printing today. I would like to attend the language club. That meets on Wednesday, not Tuesday, at a quarter past six in the evening. Please bring your passport when you register.

questions.explanation: The surname is spelled B E N T O N.
The speaker chooses River Street.
The speaker corrects Tuesday to Wednesday.
A passport is required for registration.

groups.title: Planning a field visit
groups.script: Our geography group will visit the wetlands on Friday. We had hoped to leave at eight, but the coach is only available at nine. Bring a notebook and waterproof boots. There is no need to bring lunch, because the visitor centre will provide sandwiches. The morning task is to count water birds. In the afternoon, we will compare water samples. We shall work in pairs because the equipment is limited. The final report is due on Monday, although the photographs can be sent later.

questions.explanation: The final departure time is nine.

questions.prompt: The morning task is to count _____.
questions.explanation: Bird counting is the morning task.

questions.prompt: Why will students work in pairs?
options: B. Only two students are attending.
questions.explanation: Pair work is needed because equipment is limited.
The report is due on Monday; photographs may follow.

groups.title: A changed appointment
groups.script: Hello, this is Green Dental Clinic. Your appointment was originally on Tuesday at ten. Unfortunately, the dentist will be away that morning. We can offer you Thursday at eleven thirty instead. Please call us before five today to confirm. The clinic entrance is now on Park Road, because the front door on Market Street is being repaired. You do not need to bring your old appointment letter, but please bring your identification card.

questions.prompt: The new appointment is on which day?
questions.explanation: Thursday replaces Tuesday.

questions.prompt: Which entrance should the patient use?
questions.explanation: The current entrance is on Park Road.

questions.prompt: What document should the patient bring?
questions.explanation: An identification card is requested.
The caller asks for confirmation before five today.

groups.title: A school visit
groups.script: Tomorrow, our class is visiting the science museum. Meet at the school gate at eight thirty. The bus will leave fifteen minutes later. The museum ticket is six pounds for students. Please bring a packed lunch and a bottle of water. You may take photographs in the space exhibition, but not in the laboratory. We expect to return by four. If traffic is heavy, we will send your parents a message.

questions.explanation: Students meet at eight thirty.
The ticket costs six pounds.
Photography is not allowed in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: Who will receive a message if the bus is delayed?
questions.explanation: Parents will be contacted if traffic is heavy.

groups.title: Task 1 · At least 150 words
groups.text:
The table shows the percentage of commuters using three types of transport in the fictional town of Westford. Summarise the main patterns and make relevant comparisons.

Transport | 2010 | 2020
Car | 65% | 45%
Bus | 25% | 30%
Bicycle | 10% | 25%

questions.explanation: Teacher assessment: task achievement, coherence, vocabulary, grammar.

groups.title: Task 2 · At least 250 words
groups.text: Some people believe that cities should spend more money on public transport than on new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Give reasons and relevant examples.

questions.explanation: Teacher assessment. Task 2 carries twice the weight of Task 1 in IELTS Writing.

groups.title: 1.1 · Informal email · About 50 words
groups.text: Your local sports club has announced that the swimming pool will close for two weeks for repairs. Members can use the outdoor courts during this period. The manager asks for suggestions about alternative activities. Write to a friend who also belongs to the club. Explain how you feel and suggest what you could do together.

groups.title: 1.2 · Formal email · 120–150 words
groups.text: Write to the club manager about the same situation. Explain how the closure affects you, suggest an alternative activity and ask for information about when the pool will reopen.

groups.title: 2 · Discussion post · 180–200 words
groups.text: An online discussion asks: Is it better to learn a practical skill in a group or on your own? Write a discussion post giving your view, reasons and examples.
